title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer regional failover ordering and backoff
author: Priya Nair
description:
Motivation: in the last deploy we observed increased regional failover churn and priority reordering in the SLO enforcer path. Root cause analysis pointed to a race between the per-request cancellation path and the regional backoff token refresh logic: when a connection is cancelled while a region backoff update is in-flight the enforcer could temporarily treat the region as 'degraded' twice and trigger redundant failover attempts. Secondary issue: the priority queue used for regional ordering was not stable under equal-priority items which caused unnecessary reordering during heavy load and exacerbated thrashing.

This PR contains a hotfix that addresses both issues: 1) Introduce a lightweight region-backoff mutex + per-request epoch token so cancellation handlers abort the outdated flow without flipping the region state. 2) Make the region priority queue stable by adding an insertion-sequence counter and updating the comparator to prefer older entries on tie. 3) Add a small set of unit tests that simulate cancellation races and a deterministic integration test for the enforcer queue ordering. 4) Add an integration canary config (perf-canary/fixtures/slo-enforcer-regional) used in our nightly canaries.

Changes include code-level guards (fastpaths) to keep the happy-path hot and avoid extra allocations. The fix is intentionally minimal to reduce blast radius. See commits for a concise list.

Testing: local unit/integration, CI run, and a staged canary against eu-west-1 and us-west-2 showed stable behavior for 6 hours without failover churn. Rollout plan: squash-merge to main and backport to release/2026-02.

References: Linear ENG-4821 (SLO enforcer stability), ENG-5003 (regional failover thrash), incident SUP-120 in January post-deploy.
